inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,819 logical lines. The article develops secondary zeta functions over paired nontrivial Riemann zeros through normalized Hadamard/Delta products, Mellin continuation, a shadow zeta for trivial zeros, shift-covariant Hurwitz families, and numerical continuation diagnostics. The prose is coherent, but many displayed formulas are absent or damaged in the text layer, so units retain equation-level representation dependencies and should be checked against the page image before formula-exact reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Journal cover and article front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identity, copyright notice, title, and author; no mathematical unit.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction and notation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the secondary/generalized zeta program, motivates a spectral analogy while marking its limits, maps the continuation strategy, and supplies completed-zeta and auxiliary L-series context.

sections_inspected.label: 2. General Delta and Zeta functions of order 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the abstract admissible-sequence/Delta-product framework and transfers large- and small-argument expansions through Mellin transforms to global pole and trace information.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Delta function based at s=0 and its zeta function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses functional-equation symmetry to pair zeros into a squared sequence, then derives poles, regularized determinant data, Taylor identities, special values, and a Li-coefficient connection.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Generalized Zeta functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Studies shifts of the squared-zero sequence, exposing polynomial translation behavior for polar data versus transcendental dependence of positive special values.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Symmetric base point, shadow zeta, and continuation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Moves to the symmetric zero shift, models trivial zeros and the zeta pole as a shadow spectrum, derives explicit Mellin/Hankel continuation formulas, extracts poles and trace identities, and sketches extension to other zeta/L-functions.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Hurwitz-type functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Expands general shifts around the symmetric case, derives polar and terminating trace formulas, and transfers the mechanism to two other Hurwitz-like families and their regularized products.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Recapitulation and Table 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reindexes and repeats the main analytical results and points to the new continuation and asymptotic formulas; useful as navigation, not a distinct mechanism.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A. Meromorphic Mellin transforms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the directed integration-by-parts continuation mechanism and how logarithmic asymptotic powers determine pole orders.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix B. Numerical aspects
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts density-tail acceleration with unstable numerical regularization and motivates switching to analytic continuation formulas below the direct convergence range.

sections_inspected.label: Bibliography and author information
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: References, publication dates, and affiliations; no new source argument.

accepted_units.title: Secondary zeta functions turn zero data into explicit meromorphic objects
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces Dirichlet series over paired nontrivial zeros and frames explicit continuation and special-value structure as additional information about otherwise elusive zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained opening statement; the defining displays around lines 64-80 are missing from extraction but the prose fixes their role.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equation displays (1)-(3) and the shift parameter; verify formula transcription against the page image.

accepted_units.title: The spectral analogy suggests a transfer but double poles force a separate treatment
accepted_units.why_material: Compares Riemann-zero zeta functions with spectral zeta functions and identifies the decisive mismatch: double rather than simple poles make direct trace-formula transplantation cumbersome.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the historical comparison and the explicit reason for choosing a self-contained Riemann treatment.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-grounded; several cited example formulas and parameters are extraction-damaged.

accepted_units.title: The analysis is staged by shift and half-plane because explicitness is nonuniform
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why the paper moves from an abstract framework to special shifts, a more explicit continuation at the symmetric shift, generalized shifts, Hurwitz families, and numerical appendices.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the end of the spectral-method discussion because that limitation motivates the staged program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Section and half-plane parameters survive in prose, while some displayed symbols are degraded.

accepted_units.title: Admissibility packages a zero sequence into a normalized Delta product and zeta series
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the minimal Weierstrass-product and generalized-Stirling hypotheses needed to turn a sequence into a Delta function and associated zeta function, while explaining why the framework minimizes order and pole complexity.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison with eigenvalue spectra clarifies why Delta products, rather than partition functions, are the accessible primitive for Riemann zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core assumptions and products are displayed equations (15)-(18) and are partly absent; prose supports the construction but formula-exact use needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: One Mellin transform converts asymptotics and Taylor data into complementary meromorphic continuations
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how the large-argument expansion controls poles on one side, the origin Taylor series controls positive-integer behavior on the other, and sine-factor cancellations produce trace identities and finite values.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the complete abstract transfer from Delta data to zeta poles, cancellations, and values.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mellin formulas (19)-(27), residues, and coefficients are display-dependent and require the original page for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Functional-equation pairing lowers the effective sequence order
accepted_units.why_material: Pairs functional-equation-related zeros and rewrites the completed zeta product as an even Delta product in a squared variable, replacing an awkward order-one zero sequence with a simpler order-one-half setting.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact transformed sequence is visually damaged, but the prose explicitly states the reordering, parity, convergence threshold, and change of order.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong dependence on Hadamard products (28)-(33) and the variable substitution; original formula images are needed.

accepted_units.title: Stirling expansion of the Delta product fixes the half-integer pole ladder
accepted_units.why_material: Substitutes the inverse quadratic branch into the completed-zeta asymptotics to obtain arbitrary-order Delta coefficients, double half-integer poles, values at zero, and the regularized determinant.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends where the paper flags remaining coefficients and trace values for later recovery.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-exact pole parts and constants in (34)-(40) are poorly extracted; use page images for coefficients.

accepted_units.title: Two Taylor expansions yield finite identities among zero sums, zeta derivatives, and Stieltjes cumulants
accepted_units.why_material: Matches the Delta-product Taylor series with functional-equation expansions to produce countably many three-term identities and finite decompositions for positive-integer secondary-zeta values.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the proof sketch explaining why the decomposition is finite only at the unshifted positive-integer values.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (41)-(48) carry the identities and are heavily display-dependent; prose reliably records the participants and finiteness mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Zero-sum identities connect the secondary-zeta coordinates to Li coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Records additional sum rules and a transformation linking the zero sums to Li coefficients, hence to a positivity formulation of the Riemann Hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: A compact added-in-proof bridge rather than part of the main derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The actual identities are missing in the text layer; retain only with equation-image verification.

accepted_units.title: Translation covariance separates polynomial polar data from transcendental special values
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that shifting the squared spectrum preserves admissibility and makes asymptotic coefficients, pole parts, and trace identities polynomial in the shift, while finite-point Taylor data and positive values vary transcendentally.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the normalization tradeoff between explicit Hadamard products and fully translation-covariant zeta-regularized products.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Shift formulas (49)-(54) and exact constants are display-dependent; the polynomial/transcendental dichotomy is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: The symmetric shift sacrifices an explicit constant to unlock a stronger continuation
accepted_units.why_material: Rebases the product at the most symmetric shift, notes the now-unknown normalization constant, and explains why this form is nevertheless much easier to continue meromorphically.
accepted_units.context_note: Serves as the conceptual transition into the trivial-zero shadow construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The symmetric base value and determinant equations (55)-(58) are partly stripped; verify the precise variable mapping.

accepted_units.title: Trivial zeros plus a ghost eigenvalue form a shadow spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets the gamma-factor zeros and the zeta pole as a signed auxiliary spectrum whose determinant cancels the nontrivial-zero determinant asymptotically, producing an explicit Hurwitz-type shadow zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: The endpoint contains the admissibility repair: square the linearly growing trivial-zero sequence before applying the abstract framework.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact spectrum, ghost location, and shadow-zeta formula (59)-(62) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: At the symmetric shift, resolvent terms split into explicit shadow and residual Mellin pieces
accepted_units.why_material: Uses factorization, a regularized trivial-zero resolvent, contour rotation, Hankel conversion, and residue calculus to separate an explicit shadow-zeta term from a residual integral and obtain conjugate and principal-value continuations.
accepted_units.context_note: The original v1 span contains the derivation; lines 938-969 are separately accepted as the needed interpretive context and recorded as a v1 context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: continuation formulas (63)-(74), contours, and convergence regions are not safely reconstructible from the text layer alone.

accepted_units.title: The Mellin formulas function as explicit counterparts of the zeta functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets the continuation formulas as functional-equation counterparts, compares them with Guinand and Deninger formulas, and explains why they make the left half-plane pole analysis straightforward.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides indispensable outcome and comparison context for carried unit u04.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded, with convergence half-planes and referenced formulas degraded in places.

accepted_units.title: The explicit shadow term controls poles, trace identities, and a resummed prime asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the residual integral is regular in the target half-plane, so pole and integer-value data come from the shadow term, and relates the large-negative-parameter expansion to a resummation of Guinand’s divergent prime series.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines the structural simplification with its main analytic consequences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact residues, trace identities, and asymptotic coefficients in (75)-(79) need equation-image checking.

accepted_units.title: Analyticity forces cancellation identities but leaves positive special values transcendental
accepted_units.why_material: Extracts identities by cancellation of half-integer and integer singularities in the Mellin representation, then states the boundary: key derivative values remain poorly understood even at the symmetric shift.
accepted_units.context_note: Pairs a positive mechanism with an explicit knowledge obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The identities (80)-(82) are display-dependent; prose supports the cancellation logic and limitation.

accepted_units.title: The spectral analogy is partial, and the continuation is not closed under the original zeta alone
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts pole orders with compact-surface spectra and observes that the original zeta reappears additively through the shadow term while an auxiliary Dirichlet series prevents closure.
accepted_units.context_note: Motivates the subsequent generalization rather than merely cataloguing differences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-grounded; parameter values and formula references should be checked visually.

accepted_units.title: Functional equations generate a reusable continuation template for zeta and L-series combinations
accepted_units.why_material: Abstracts the Mellin continuation to Dirichlet zeta/L-series with controlled poles and functional equations, applies it to the auxiliary beta series, and adds or subtracts formulas to trade multiplicative inputs for simpler additive shadow terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Gaussian-integer zeta example and an explicit identity obtained only after combining two continuation systems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The general template (84)-(90), gamma factors, and combined formulas are display-dependent and need page-image verification.

accepted_units.title: Expansion around the symmetric shift transports poles finitely but not all special values
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the general shifted zeta around the symmetric case, deriving finite polar and negative-integer trace formulas while explaining why positive-value data at the other special shift require infinite, transcendental expansions.
accepted_units.context_note: Makes precise that the two favored shifts are complementary rather than one superseding the other.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Binomial expansion and polar formulas (91)-(96) are equation-dependent; prose establishes termination and complementarity.

accepted_units.title: Expansion and cancellation reduce two more singular Hurwitz families to the symmetric secondary zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers the shift-expansion method to a more singular family, shows cancellations leaving a single pole in Deninger’s family, and interprets the derivative at zero as conversion from a zeta-regularized product to Hadamard form under universal normalization rules.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with the structural parallel between the two Hurwitz-like families.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact pole residues, finite values, and product formula (97)-(102) require the original equation images.

accepted_units.title: Directed integrations by parts turn asymptotic log powers into meromorphic pole orders
accepted_units.why_material: Supplies the omitted proof mechanism behind the Mellin continuation: sequential integration by parts crosses exponent boundaries, logarithmic terms raise pole order, and the origin expansion gives continuation in the opposite direction.
accepted_units.context_note: A general reusable proof schema underlying Section 2 rather than a new Riemann-specific result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (103)-(110) are damaged, but the stepwise logic and log-degree-to-pole-order rule survive in prose.

accepted_units.title: The symmetric and original secondary zetas are numerically close for a structural scale reason
accepted_units.why_material: Explains the observed closeness by the dominance of squared zero ordinates over the shift and quantifies the first correction heuristically, while explicitly noting the numerical use of the Riemann Hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: Heuristic evidence only; it is not an analytic or formal consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Numerical expressions and constants are partially damaged; consult Table 2 and page image before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Density-tail acceleration fails at a fluctuation barrier, prompting analytic continuation
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces a slowly convergent tail by an integrated zero-density estimate, identifies the later obstruction from erratic zero fluctuations, tests Cesàro damping, and recommends the continuation formulas when regularization becomes unstable.
accepted_units.context_note: Distinguishes acceleration of the dominant trend from uncontrolled damping of fluctuations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Euler-Maclaurin-like remainder and tabulated evaluations are display-dependent; prose safely supports the diagnostic and method switch.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Delta-to-shadow continuation pipeline
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A functional-equation-symmetric product turns zero data into an admissible Delta object; Mellin continuation then separates an explicit trivial-zero shadow from a residual nontrivial-zero integral.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-internal method synthesis, not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, and exact formulas remain scan-dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two complementary special shifts
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: One shift makes positive special values unusually explicit, while the symmetric shift makes left-half-plane continuation and polar data unusually explicit; neither dominates globally.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The complementarity is established for the families and representations treated here, not for arbitrary zero statistics.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic continuation as a numerical regularizer
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: When direct zero sums cross from slow convergence into fluctuation-dominated instability, the source replaces increasingly severe summability prescriptions with an independently derived continuation formula.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical discussion is heuristic, uses finitely many zeros, and assumes the observed zeros lie on the critical line.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Combination trades multiplicative complexity for additive simplicity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Adding or subtracting continuation formulas for related L-functions can simplify the additive shadow term only by changing the multiplicative zeta object under the residual integral.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Demonstrated through the specific zeta, beta, and Gaussian-integer examples in the source; no general closure theorem is supplied.
